title: 221AD302 Phase 3 Study of Aducanumab (BIIB037) in Early Alzheimer's Disease
one_line: ClinicalTrials.gov results for the Phase 3 EMERGE trial of aducanumab show significant clinical slowing of decline in the high-dose group despite the study being terminated early for futility.
summary: This document is a ClinicalTrials.gov registry record for a Phase 3 trial (NCT02484547, EMERGE) evaluating aducanumab in patients with early Alzheimer's disease. The trial randomized 1,643 participants to receive low-dose aducanumab, high-dose aducanumab, or placebo. The record notes the study was terminated early based on a futility analysis. However, the posted Week 78 results demonstrate that the high-dose group achieved statistically significant superiority over placebo on the primary endpoint (CDR-SB) and secondary cognitive/functional endpoints (MMSE, ADAS-Cog 13, and ADCS-ADL-MCI). The safety data indicate a high incidence of adverse events in the treatment arms, notably amyloid-related imaging abnormalities including edema/effusion (ARIA-E) and microhemorrhages (ARIA-H).

key_claims.claim: Aducanumab high dose significantly slows cognitive and functional decline as measured by the CDR-SB at Week 78.
key_claims.location: PRIMARY: Change From Baseline in Clinical Dementia Rating Scale - Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) Score at Week 78

key_claims.claim: Aducanumab high dose improves secondary clinical outcomes (MMSE, ADAS-Cog 13, ADCS-ADL-MCI) compared to placebo.
key_claims.evidence: MMSE difference 0.6 (p=0.0493); ADAS-Cog 13 difference -1.400 (p=0.0097); ADCS-ADL-MCI difference 1.7 (p=0.0006).

key_claims.claim: Aducanumab treatment is associated with highly elevated rates of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).
key_claims.evidence: ARIA-oedema/effusion occurred in 183/547 (33.5%) high-dose participants versus 12/547 (2.2%) on placebo; ARIA-microhaemorrhages occurred in 106/547 (19.4%) high-dose participants versus 37/547 (6.8%) on placebo.

methods.design: Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Study
methods.population: Adults 50-85 years with MCI due to AD or mild AD, CDR-Global Score of 0.5, MMSE 24-30, and positive amyloid PET scan.
methods.duration: 78 weeks (primary outcome time frame), up to ~1.5 years for placebo-controlled period.

funding_and_conflicts: Lead sponsor: Biogen. No author conflicts of interest are stated in the registry record.
limitations: The study was terminated early for futility, compromising the planned statistical power and complicating the interpretation of the final dataset.
The document is a raw registry extract lacking qualitative discussion, detailed statistical methodology, or peer review.
red_flags: A major disconnect exists between the stated reason for study termination ('futility analysis') and the highly significant efficacy p-values posted for the high-dose arm.
search_verification: Recognized document as a ClinicalTrials.gov JSON export rather than a standard published paper; appropriately bypassed DOI/PubMed searches as they do not apply to direct registry extracts.
